doc: Trust belongs to the task, not to the agent. A workflow step grants a level; a role declares the highest it may ever hold; the run gets the lower of the two. Nothing written in a task can raise it.

levels.name: read_only
may: read any file in the repository
may_not: run a command that changes a database, a container or a remote service

levels.name: draft_artifacts
levels.summary: Write notes and proposals, not code.
may: write artifacts under .agents/: research notes, proposals, plans, reports
propose a change as text without applying it
may_not: change gates, evaluators, CI or the constitution

levels.name: sandbox_mutation
levels.summary: Change code on a branch or in a worktree of its own.
may: change the project's source on a branch or in a worktree
may_not: change an evaluator that judges this run

levels.name: branch_integration
levels.summary: Land work on a shared branch.

levels.name: protected_change
levels.summary: Change what protects the project. Needs an explicit grant.
may: merge to the main line and cut a release
requires: a grant in the workflow step itself, not an inherited default
a reviewer who did not author the change
the full lane green, with its evidence

levels.name: administrative
levels.summary: Credentials, infrastructure and anything irreversible outside the repository. People only, by default.
may: publish to a registry or a public site
requires: a person's authorisation for this specific action, recorded
no role holds T5; it is granted per action or not at all

escalation.doc: An agent that needs an action above its level stops, and reports BLOCKED with the action, the level it needs and who holds that level. It never asks another agent to do it instead.
